links.outcome: Non-specialist physician vignette test scores before vs after reviewing AI outputs
links.effect: Median per-round score (0-10) rose from 5.5 to 8.0 for GPT-4 (Δ=3.0, p<0.001) and from 6.0 to 8.0 for DeepSeek (Δ=2.5, p<0.001); between-model difference p=0.781.
links.quote: After reviewing AI answers, non‑specialist physicians' case‑based test scores improved significantly: median per‑round score (0-10) increased from 5.5 to 8.0 for GPT‑4 (Δ=3.0, p<0.001) and from 6.0 to 8.0 for DeepSeek (Δ=2.5, p<0.001).

links.outcome: Presence of red-flag/referral triggers and safety omissions in LLM IBD guidance
links.effect: Both models showed inconsistent red-flag/referral triggers and safety omissions; no harmful recommendations were identified.
links.quote: Across both models, common limitations included limited patient‑level individualization, inconsistent red‑flag/referral triggers, and lack of verifiable, time‑stamped references; no harmful recommendations were identified, but safety omissions were present in both models.

links.outcome: Verifiability of references cited in LLM outputs
links.effect: Both models lacked verifiable, time-stamped references.
links.quote: Across both models, common limitations included limited patient‑level individualization, inconsistent red‑flag/referral triggers, and lack of verifiable, time‑stamped references; no harmful recommendations were identified, but safety omissions were present in both models.

screen.reason: The study empirically tests the effect of providing AI guidance to non-specialist physicians versus unassisted practice on clinical vignette management scores in a pre-post crossover experiment.
